title: Beyond Chatbots - The Anatomy of an Autonomous Agent
core_concept: The difference between passive LLM query-response and autonomous agents. The ReAct loop (Perception, Working Memory, Planning, Action, Reflection). Designing for deterministic execution.
homework: Draft the architectural block diagram of your dream assistant: separate brain, memory, tools, and sensors.

title: Choosing the Brain - Local Engines vs Cloud APIs
core_concept: Local inference (Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp, quantized GGUF models) vs Frontier Cloud APIs (Gemini 2.5/3.8, Claude 3.5, GPT-4o). Latency, privacy guarantees, inference cost at scale, and hybrid routing architectures.
homework: Set up a local LLM runner (like Ollama or vLLM) alongside a cloud API key, and benchmark inference time per token.

title: The System Prompt as an Operating System Kernel
core_concept: Metaprompting, behavioral contracts, state machines defined in system prompts, and setting defensive boundaries against prompt injection.
homework: Write your assistant's core 'Kernel Prompt' defining strict behavioral boundaries and input-output contracts.

title: Context Window Dynamics and Attention Degradation
core_concept: The mechanics of transformer attention: the 'Lost in the Middle' phenomenon, needle-in-a-haystack limits, token budgets, and why bigger context windows are not an excuse for bad memory hygiene.
homework: Calculate your agent's maximum prompt overhead (system prompt + tool schemas) and define a strict working budget.

title: Structured Outputs and API Contracts
core_concept: Why free-form text breaks software pipelines. Pydantic models, JSON Schema generation, constrained decoding, and guaranteed schema compliance for tool calling.
homework: Create a Pydantic schema for an agent action command and enforce valid JSON output from your model.

title: The Base Codebase Architecture
core_concept: Setting up the project repository: directory layout, event-driven architecture, internal telemetry, and logging the agent's internal monologue and tool trace.
homework: Initialize the Git repo with a modular folder structure: /core, /memory, /tools, and /interfaces.

title: The Memory Hierarchy - From Registers to Cold Storage
core_concept: Cognitive architectures: working memory, ephemeral scratchpads, short-term episodic memory, and persistent semantic storage.
homework: Map out which user data belongs in working memory vs vector storage vs persistent relational records.

title: Short-Term Episodic Memory and Context Compaction
core_concept: Sliding window buffers, rolling summaries, pruning obsolete tool responses, and dynamic context compaction without losing key facts.
homework: Implement a rolling summary function that compresses chat history every 10 turns.

title: Long-Term Vector Memory - Semantic Embeddings Deep Dive
core_concept: Embedding models (MTEB leaderboard), cosine similarity, semantic chunking algorithms, chunk overlap, and vector dimensionality tradeoffs.
homework: Write a chunking script that splits your personal notes based on Markdown headings rather than arbitrary character counts.

title: Vector Databases in Practice - Choosing Local Simplicity
core_concept: Evaluating vector stores: SQLite-vec vs Chroma vs LanceDB vs pgvector. Why embedding vectors directly into local SQLite beats heavy cloud databases for personal agents.
homework: Set up a local SQLite-vec or Chroma instance and store your first 100 embedded personal notes.

title: Hybrid Search and Cross-Encoder Re-Ranking
core_concept: Why pure vector search fails on keyword lookups (names, serial numbers, dates). Combining BM25 keyword search with dense embeddings, plus secondary re-ranking with cross-encoders.
homework: Implement a Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) algorithm combining BM25 and vector similarity scores.

title: Graph Memory and Knowledge Graphs (GraphRAG)
core_concept: When vector similarity is not enough: nodes, entities, and directed relationships. Storing temporal knowledge (e.g., 'Sophie moved to Amsterdam in 2024') in an entity graph.
homework: Create a simple entity-relation JSON table connecting your key contacts, projects, and recurring commitments.

title: Passive Profile Extraction - Teaching the Agent to Learn You
core_concept: Running background reflection prompts that scan daily user interactions to passively extract personal facts, communication preferences, and habits.
homework: Build an extraction prompt that outputs structured profile updates from a raw conversation.

title: Function Calling Mechanics - Giving the Model Hands
core_concept: How LLMs switch from language tokens to tool invocation tokens. The tool execution loop: schema declaration, model dispatch, local code execution, and observation feedback.
homework: Write a raw tool definition for a local weather function and execute the model's tool call response.

title: Designing Fault-Tolerant, Self-Healing Tools
core_concept: Defensive tool engineering: strict type coercion, detailed error messages fed back to the LLM for self-correction, and retry policies for flaky external APIs.
homework: Implement a tool handler that intercepts JSONDecode errors and asks the LLM to auto-correct the arguments.

title: Connecting the Core Productivity Stack - Calendar & Time
core_concept: Integrating Google Calendar / CalDAV: time-zone arithmetic, resolving relative time ('next Tuesday at 3pm'), handling conflicts, and programmatic availability calculations.
homework: Connect a calendar API tool and prompt your agent to find open 45-minute slots tomorrow afternoon.

title: Email and Communication Pipelines
core_concept: IMAP/SMTP vs modern REST APIs (Gmail/Outlook). The crucial policy difference between 'Drafting' and 'Sending', plus automated triage, labeling, and summarization.
homework: Build an automated inbox triage script that classifies unread emails into: Action Required, Informational, or Spam.

title: Note Systems & Digital Brain Synchronization
core_concept: Interfacing with your second brain (Obsidian vaults, local Markdown files, Notion API). Parsing frontmatter, appending daily log entries, and automated bi-directional indexing.
homework: Write an agent tool that appends structured meeting notes directly to a daily Markdown file.

title: Live Web Search and Headless Browser Scraping
core_concept: Augmenting the agent with real-time web capabilities using Tavily, Serper, and headless Playwright. Cleaning HTML DOM to preserve tokens while extracting relevant data.
homework: Build a web research tool that searches a topic, fetches the top URL, and returns clean Markdown.

title: Safety Architectures and Human-in-the-Loop (HITL)
core_concept: Principle of least privilege for agents: separating read-only queries from mutating/destructive operations. Implementing approval gates via CLI or smartphone confirmations.
homework: Create a permission decorator `@requires_approval` that pauses execution on destructive tool actions.

title: Autonomous Planning - ReAct, Plan-and-Solve, and DAGs
core_concept: Advanced cognitive patterns: ReAct vs Plan-and-Solve. Decomposing complex goals into Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) and dynamic replanning when tools fail.
homework: Prompt your agent to decompose a broad goal ('Plan a 3-day tech workshop') into a sequential dependency tree.

title: State Machines and Orchestration Frameworks
core_concept: State-driven execution: LangGraph vs LlamaIndex Workflows vs raw Python state machines. Managing execution checkpoints, rollbacks, and persistent session state.
homework: Build a 3-node state machine (Plan -> Execute -> Reflect) in pure Python.

title: Multi-Agent Specialization - The Router and Specialist Pattern
core_concept: Why monolithic single agents fail on complex tasks. Designing an Orchestrator/Router that delegates to specialized sub-agents (e.g., Researcher, Coder, Scheduler, Secretary).
homework: Implement a router agent that inspects incoming queries and dispatches to either a 'Personal Data Agent' or 'Coding Agent'.

title: Inter-Agent Communication and Shared Blackboards
core_concept: Communication topologies between sub-agents: shared blackboard memory vs direct peer-to-peer message passing. Preventing agent debate loops and infinite ping-pongs.
homework: Create a shared blackboard dictionary where Agent A posts findings and Agent B reads them to synthesize an answer.

title: Sandboxed Code Execution
core_concept: Allowing your agent to write and execute Python scripts to solve data problems. Isolating code execution via Docker containers, WebAssembly (Wasm), or cloud sandboxes (E2B).
homework: Spin up a local Docker container or Python sandbox where your agent can safely execute math scripts.

title: Computer Use and Desktop Automation
core_concept: Anthropic Computer Use and OS-level automation: taking screenshots, coordinate calculation, and programmatic mouse/keyboard events. Safety precautions and speed limitations.
homework: Test an open-source screen-capture script that crops and resizes screenshots for model inspection.

title: Proactive Background Triggers and Heartbeat Daemons
core_concept: Moving from reactive (answering user prompts) to proactive (acting autonomously). Setting up heartbeat crons, monitoring incoming data streams, and event-driven wakeups.
homework: Write a 15-minute cron daemon that wakes your agent to inspect your calendar and send an alert if a meeting is in 30 minutes.

title: Loop Detection, Hallucination Guards, and Self-Correction
core_concept: How to detect when an agent is stuck in repetitive tool-call loops. Maximum hop counters, token-budget circuit breakers, and automated self-correction prompts.
homework: Implement a sliding history hash-checker that terminates execution if the same tool call with identical arguments occurs 3 times.

title: Low-Latency Voice Architecture
core_concept: Deconstructing voice assistant pipelines: Speech-to-Text (Whisper, Deepgram) -> LLM streaming -> Text-to-Speech (Gemini TTS, ElevenLabs). Breaking through the sub-500ms latency barrier.
homework: Stream text chunks directly from your LLM response into an audio player without waiting for full completion.

title: Native Multimodal Models vs Modular Pipelines
core_concept: Analyzing end-to-end multimodal audio models (Gemini Live WebSocket / OpenAI Realtime) vs modular pipelines (Whisper + LLM + TTS). Tradeoffs in control, tool invocation, and conversational interruption.
homework: Connect a local microphone stream to an audio WebSocket endpoint.

title: Vision and Ambient Perception
core_concept: Giving your assistant eyes: integrating webcam snapshots, processing incoming screenshots, multimodal document extraction, and spatial visual reasoning.
homework: Write a function that grabs a snapshot from your webcam and asks your multimodal model: 'What am I working on right now?'

title: The Always-On Home Hub - Hardware & Self-Hosting
core_concept: Hardware selection for 24/7 self-hosting: Apple Silicon Mac Mini vs Intel NUC vs Raspberry Pi 5. Systemd services, memory management, thermal throttling, and automatic restart daemons.
homework: Configure your assistant project to run as an automated system service (`systemd` on Linux or `launchd` on macOS).

title: Remote Mobile Access - Tunnels, WireGuard & iOS Shortcuts
core_concept: Connecting your phone to your home agent securely without opening public firewall ports: Tailscale mesh networking, local API gateways, and iOS Shortcuts / Action Button integration.
homework: Set up a Tailscale node on your host machine and test triggering a local agent webhook from your iPhone.

title: Agent Evals and Continuous Benchmarking
core_concept: How to prevent regression: building automated eval suites. Testing tool call accuracy, memory recall precision, and latency budgets on every codebase change.
homework: Write a 5-test benchmark script that verifies your agent correctly calls the calendar tool across various tricky phrasing styles.

title: The Sovereign Future - Assembly, Fine-Tuning, and Evolution
core_concept: The complete architecture unified: a sovereign assistant that possesses local memory, multi-tool mastery, voice perception, and private execution. Looking ahead to self-improving agents and fine-tuning on personal history.
homework: Celebrate! Conduct an end-to-end audit of your completed assistant pipeline.
